items.actClause:
AN ACT relating to authorizing the state university of New York at Stony Brook
to lease certain lands for the purpose of constructing a facility to support
research and development to address the national semiconductor chip shortage
and related environmental sustainability issues
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9614

SPONSOR: MARTINEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act relating to authorizing the state university of New York at Stony
Brook to lease certain lands for the purpose of constructing a facility
to support research and development to address the national semiconduc-
tor chip shortage and related environmental sustainability issues

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to authorize Stony Brook University
to lease certain lands for the purpose of constructing a facility to
support research and development of semiconductor chips.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Legislative findings.

Section 2. Authorizes SUNY Trustees to lease a portion of university
property for the purpose of developing a semiconductor chip facility.

Section 3. Any contract/lease entered shall be deemed to be a state
contract for the purposes of article 15a of the executive law.

Section 4. All work performed shall be deemed public work and shall be
subject to provisions of article 8 of the labor law and in the same
manner as a contract of the state.  All provisions of article 8 of the
labor law shall be required including the enforcement of prevailing wage
requirements by the fiscal officer as defined in paragraph e of subdivi-
sion 5 of section 220 of the labor law.

Section 5. Ensures the state university of New York shall not contract
out to the ground lessee or any subsidiary for the instruction or any
pedagogical functions or services, or any administrative services, and
similar professional services currently being performed by state employ-
ees at Stony Brook.

Section 6. Provides definitions to "project" and "project labor agree-
ment".

Section 7. Provides that the ground lessee may require a contractor
awarded a contract, subcontract, lease, grant, bond, covenant or other
agreement for a project to enter into a project labor agreement during
and for the work involved with such project when such requirement is
part of the ground lessee's request for proposals for the project and
when the state university of New York at Stony Brook determines that the
record supporting the decision to enter into such an agreement estab-
lishes that the interest underlying the competitive bidding laws are
best met by requiring a project labor agreement obtaining the best work
at the lowest possible price; preventing favoritism, fraud and
corruption; the impact of delay; the possibility of cost savings; and
any local history of labor unrest.

Section 8. This act shall not be deemed to waive or impair any rights or
benefits of state employees.


Section 9. The terms and conditions may provide for the obtaining of
funding or financing, whether public or private, unsecured, or secured
(including, but not limited to, secured by leasehold mortgages and
assignments of rents and leases), by the ground lessee and parties
contracting with the ground lessee for the purposes of completing the
project.

Section 10. Such a lease shall include an indemnity provision.

Section 11. Any contract shall be awarded by a competitive process.

Section 12. Provides the metes and bounds for the 8 acres of land situ-
ated on Stony Brook's Research and Development Park.

Section 13. The land cannot be leased after 5 years of the effective
date.

Section 14. If the provisions of this are inconsistent with the
provisions of any law, the provisions of this act shall be controlling.

Section 15. Sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Stony Brook University is one of the State's flagship institutions,
which strives to spur innovation and support economic development for
the State. Veeco is a global company that builds the equipment needed
for the semiconductor industry. The company has outgrown its current
headquarters and manufacturing facility in Plainview and is seeking to
relocate to the University's Research and Development Park (R&D Park).
The R&D Park is zoned for up to ten buildings with three, currently
built (including its two Centers of Excellence), a fourth in development
and Veeco would be the fifth building.

By relocating to Stony Brook, Veeco will ensure its skilled workforce
will remain in New York and Stony Brook and Veeco wilt develop a signif-
icant talent pipeline to support high end manufacturing and cutting edge
research to ensure New York is at the forefront of the semiconductor
industry.  This legislation is necessary to provide a ground lease to
enable Veeco to build its new facility at Stony Brook's R&D Park.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER: S9614B

SPONSOR: MARTINEZ

to lease certain lands for the purpose of constructing a facility to
support research and development of semiconductor chips.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Legislative findings.

Section 2. The state university of New York trustees are authorized and
empowered, without any public bidding, to lease and otherwise contract
to make available to a not-for-profit corporation, established by or
affiliated with Stony Brook University, an educational corporation or
any other person (other than the state government or any agency thereof
or any public authority) a portion of the lands of the university gener-
ally described in this act for the purpose of developing, constructing,
maintaining and operating a facility to engage in its private commercial
research, development and manufacturing purposes, while additionally
providing dedicated space which will support the research and develop-
ment needs of faculty, staff, students, and the community, which may
include supporting services to address the national semiconductor chip
shortage and related environmental sustainability issues.
